headline: Waller and hawkish minutes crush metals; inventory builds sink oil and flatten the Treasury curve
summary: Fed hawks set the tone: Waller floated a 50bp December hike and the October minutes showed almost all officials expect more increases, lifting the dollar and sending gold down about 3% and silver about 5% to 14-month lows. Bigger-than-expected US crude and gasoline builds knocked WTI 3.2% to a three-month low and RBOB to its lowest since early March. Cheaper oil pulled long Treasury yields down while the 2-year edged up, and European bonds ended near flat after a firmer core inflation revision.
drivers: Waller and the minutes revive bigger-hike talk

Waller said a 50bp hike or a stronger signal may be needed to stop 3% inflation becoming the norm, and the minutes said a couple of officials saw room for more than 25bp in December. Markets moved to about 27bp priced for December and about 62bp over three meetings.
Inventory builds push oil to a three-month low

The EIA showed crude stocks up 3.4m barrels against a near-flat forecast and gasoline up 5.2m against 1.6m expected. Dec WTI settled $2.75 lower at $83.26, its lowest since Aug 26, and Brent fell $1.19 to $91.95.
Metals break down on the dollar and real rates

Spot gold fell about $126, or 3.3%, to near $3,723, its lowest since September 2025, and silver lost about 5% to near $45. Gulf tensions brought no haven demand as the dollar held near a 19-month high.

The 2-year rose about 1.5bp to 4.80% while the 10-year fell about 3.5bp to 5.07% and the 30-year about 5bp to 5.41% as oil slid; a 20-year sale at 5.459% was average. Bunds and OATs finished near flat after euro-area core inflation was revised up to 2.6%.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled -$2.75 (-3.2%) at $83.26, lowest since Aug 26, after losing over $4 intraday; Brent -$1.19 at $91.95.
oil.why: The EIA reported a 3.4m-barrel crude build to 417.8m against a Reuters poll of about 58,000 barrels, plus a 5.2m-barrel gasoline build and a 1.6m-barrel distillate build, confirming the surplus story after a large API build the night before. Ongoing US-Iran incidents around Hormuz gave little support, and a firmer dollar on hawkish Fed talk added pressure. A 1.2m-barrel Cushing draw was the only bullish detail.
oil.outlook: Bias lower in an $80–87 range now that $84 has broken; a settle under $82 opens the high $70s. A real Hormuz disruption or OPEC+ restraint on Nov 29 would bring $87–90 back.
oil.watch: Dec WTI expiry Thu Nov 19, Gulf shipping headlines and OPEC+ Nov 29.

gas.note: Dec RBOB fell 5.30¢ (-2.1%) to $2.4819, a fourth straight loss and the lowest settle since Mar 3.
gas.why: Gasoline led the energy complex lower after the EIA showed a 5.2m-barrel stock build to 215.9m, more than three times the 1.6m expected, as cheaper winter blends and soft autumn demand meet recovering supply. RBOB has dropped about 19¢ in four sessions and roughly 25% this month. The pump price is following: AAA's national average fell to about $3.75, around 19¢ lower in a week.
gas.outlook: Bias lower in a $2.38–2.58 range while stocks rebuild and cracks stay soft; a move back above $2.60 would need WTI above $88 or a refinery outage.
gas.watch: EIA stocks Wed Nov 25, AAA's daily average into Thanksgiving and the Dec contract's late-November expiry.

gold.note: Spot fell about $126 (-3.3%) to near $3,723, after a low of $3,719, the weakest since September 2025.
gold.why: Gold broke its year low as Fed hawks pushed the policy outlook higher: Waller argued for a 50bp hike or a stronger signal, and the October minutes showed almost all officials see further increases, with a couple open to more than 25bp in December. The 2-year yield rose and the dollar held near a 19-month high, raising the cost of holding a non-yielding asset. Fresh US-Iran tensions brought no haven demand, and broad commodity selling added pressure.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,630–3,800 range while hike pricing keeps rising; a close under $3,719 targets about $3,650. Reclaiming $3,780 on softer data or a weaker dollar would steady it.
gold.watch: Jobless claims Thu Nov 19, flash PMIs Fri Nov 20 and Fed speakers.

silver.note: Spot dropped about 5% to near $45, after touching $44.64, the lowest in more than a year.
silver.why: Silver fell harder than gold because it carries both the rate hit and the industrial-demand worry: hawkish Fed talk lifted the dollar and short-term yields, while broad commodity selling and a weak materials sector hurt its growth link. Tuesday's short-covering bounce reversed fully, and the gold-silver ratio widened back toward 83 from about 81.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $43–47 range; a close below $44 opens about $41. A softer dollar and a recovery in chip stocks would be needed to regain $46.5–47.
silver.watch: Jobless claims Thu Nov 19, flash PMIs Fri Nov 20 and the dollar.

us2y.note: Up about 1.5bp to near 4.80%, as 2s10s flattened about 5bp to near 26bp.
us2y.why: The front end sold off as Fed officials leaned harder against inflation: Waller made the case for a 50bp move or a firmer signal, Daly and Barr backed more hikes, and the minutes said a couple of officials saw room for more than 25bp in December. December pricing rose to about 27bp and about 62bp over three meetings. Stronger housing starts of 1.309m against 1.245m expected added to the move.
us2y.outlook: Range of 4.74–4.90% with an upward bias while 50bp talk lingers; a strong claims or PMI print would test 4.90%, while a deeper equity slump could pull it back toward 4.74%.
us2y.watch: Jobless claims Thu Nov 19, flash PMIs Fri Nov 20 and Fed speakers.

us5y.note: Down about 1.5bp to near 4.89%, as the belly sat between a higher 2-year and a lower long end.
us5y.why: The belly split the difference between hawkish Fed news and falling oil. Waller's 50bp talk and the minutes pushed up near-term hike pricing, but WTI's 3% drop to a three-month low eased inflation expectations further out. The net effect was a small rally of about 1.5bp.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.82–4.98% with a neutral bias; firm data that lock in a larger December move would lift it toward 4.98%, while oil under $80 would bring 4.82%.
us5y.watch: Jobless claims Thu Nov 19, flash PMIs and Fed speakers.

us10y.note: Down about 3.5bp to near 5.07%, after trading near 5.12% before the oil slide.
us10y.why: The 10-year fell as oil dropped 3% on large EIA inventory builds, easing inflation fears, and investors read more Fed tightening now as less inflation later. Hawkish minutes and Waller's 50bp case lifted the front end instead, flattening the curve. A 20-year auction that stopped right on the when-issued level at 5.459%, with a 2.63 bid-to-cover, kept supply worries in check.
us10y.outlook: Range of 5.00–5.15% with a mild downward bias while oil slides and the Fed sounds firm; a close below 5.00% needs oil near $80, and a break above 5.15% would need hot data.
us10y.watch: Jobless claims Thu Nov 19, flash PMIs Fri Nov 20 and oil.

us30y.note: Down about 5bp to near 5.41%, leading the rally as 2s30s flattened about 6bp.
us30y.why: The long bond outperformed as cheaper oil and a more aggressive Fed both lowered long-run inflation risk. The 20-year sale cleared at 5.459% with no tail and indirect bidders taking about 60%, a calm result after last week's weak 30-year auction. A Treasury buyback that took only about $1.2bn of a $6bn target was a reminder of thin liquidity.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.35–5.50% with a neutral bias; further oil weakness could reach 5.35%, while a renewed term-premium push or hot data would bring 5.50% back.
us30y.watch: Jobless claims Thu Nov 19, flash PMIs and next week's supply calendar.

de2y.note: Up about 1–2bp to near 3.14%, reversing an early dip after core inflation was revised up.
de2y.why: Short Bunds rallied early with the risk-off tone, then gave the gains back when Eurostat confirmed October inflation at 4.0% and revised core up to 2.6% from 2.5%, with energy at 21%. That supports about 91% odds of an ECB hike on Dec 17, and hawkish US Fed minutes and Waller's 50bp talk added late pressure.
de2y.outlook: Range of 3.08–3.20% with a mild upward bias while a December hike is priced; weak flash PMIs or oil below $80 would bring 3.08%.
de2y.watch: Euro-area flash PMIs Fri Nov 20, ECB Governing Council Nov 25 and the ECB Dec 17.

de5y.note: About flat near 3.19%, after an early dip.
de5y.why: The belly balanced a firmer core inflation revision to 2.6% and hawkish Fed news against cheaper oil, which eases the energy-led inflation that has driven ECB hike bets. European stocks fell about 1%, which supported bonds early, but the bid faded as the US curve flattened.
de5y.outlook: Range of 3.12–3.25% with a neutral bias; hawkish ECB comments would test 3.25%, while weak PMIs and lower oil would bring 3.12%.
de5y.watch: Flash PMIs Fri Nov 20 and ECB speakers.

de10y.note: About flat near 3.38%, after dipping to about 3.35% in the morning.
de10y.why: Bunds rallied early, with the 10-year down almost 4bp to 3.35%, as stocks fell and oil slid, then the gains faded after the core inflation revision and hawkish signals from the Fed. The ECB's Financial Stability Review warned about AI valuations and high public debt but signalled no hurry to support bond markets.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.30–3.45% with a neutral bias; lower oil caps yields, while a break above 3.45% would need US 10-year yields back above 5.15%.
de10y.watch: Flash PMIs Fri Nov 20, German supply and US data.

de30y.note: About flat near 3.75%, holding near recent highs.
de30y.why: The long end moved little because heavy German borrowing plans keep term premium high, offsetting the support from lower oil and weak stocks. The ECB's warning about high public debt in large economies also kept long-dated buyers cautious.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.68–3.82% with a mild upward bias; a break above 3.82% would need weak German auctions or US 30-year yields above 5.50%.
de30y.watch: German supply, flash PMIs and US long-end moves.

fr2y.note: Down about 1bp to near 3.61%, steady against Schatz.
fr2y.why: Short OATs held firm as early risk-off flows offset the upward revision to euro-area core inflation. ECB pricing changed little, with a December hike about 91% priced, so moves at the front end stayed small.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.54–3.68% with a neutral bias while hike pricing holds; a sustained oil drop that cools inflation would bring 3.54%.
fr2y.watch: Flash PMIs Fri Nov 20 and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Up about 1bp to near 4.28%, lagging Bunds slightly.
fr5y.why: Middle OATs underperformed slightly after the ECB's Financial Stability Review singled out France, saying markets can help discipline indebted governments and signalling no hurry to intervene. Le Pen's plans to scrap the Macron pension reform also keep fiscal doubts alive, though the Senate's passage of the social security budget helped limit losses.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.20–4.35% with a neutral bias; budget progress would pull it toward 4.20%, while a government crisis or poor polls would lift it toward 4.35%.
fr5y.watch: Budget debate in parliament, presidential polls and flash PMIs.

fr10y.note: About flat near 4.88% after dipping to about 4.85%; spread to Bunds near 150bp.
fr10y.why: OATs rallied early with Bunds, then faded after the ECB said market discipline can help push indebted states like France to cut spending and that it is in no hurry to step in. The Senate's approval of the 2027 social security budget eased some passage risk, which kept the spread near 150bp, close to its recent range and below October's 177bp peak.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.80–4.95% with the spread at about 145–158bp; budget progress could tighten it toward 145bp, while a government crisis or weak polling would push it above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: Budget debate, presidential polls and the Dec 9 Senate vote.

fr30y.note: Down about 1bp to near 5.42%, now about level with the US 30-year.
fr30y.why: Long OATs edged lower with global long ends as oil fell, though the ECB's warning on high debt limited the rally. France's 10-year now yields more than Italy's, and political risk before the 2027 election keeps a premium in long maturities.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.35–5.50% with a neutral bias; a credible budget path could take it toward 5.35%, while a political setback or US 30-year yields above 5.50% would lift it toward 5.50%.
fr30y.watch: Budget debate, presidential polls and US long-end moves.

watch: Next: Dec WTI expiry, jobless claims and Anthropic's IPO Thu Nov 19; flash PMIs Fri Nov 20; ECB Governing Council Nov 25 and EIA stocks the same day; OPEC+ Nov 29, then the Fed Dec 8–9 and ECB Dec 17.
